skills.name: Precise Multi-Constraint Execution
skills.description: The agent understands what is requested but executes with incorrect parameters: wrong target object, wrong payment method, wrong item variant selected, or applies a change to the wrong sub-element of a compound entity (e.g., modifying outbound flights when only the return was requested). This is a precision failure at the level of API argument construction.
skills.reasoning: Across both domains, the agent consistently identifies the correct tool to call but constructs its arguments from the wrong element of a complex request — e.g., keeping outbound flights in round-trip changes when only the return was targeted, or returning to the wrong payment method despite explicit user instruction.

skills.name: Sequential API State Dependency
skills.description: The agent fails to track how one tool call changes system state in ways that affect subsequent calls. It either calls tools in an order that invalidates later operations (e.g., issuing a return that marks an order as 'return requested' and then trying to exchange items from the same order), or makes repeated math/payment-calculation errors across multi-step transactions.
skills.reasoning: In retail task R19, the agent returned items first (changing order status to 'return requested') and then attempted an exchange on the same order, which the system rejected. In airline tasks A17 and A20, the agent repeatedly failed to compute correct payment totals across certificate/gift-card/credit-card splits, causing cascading errors.

skills.name: Complete Multi-Step Task Execution
skills.description: When a user requests several distinct operations in a single conversation, the agent completes some but omits others, either stopping after partial execution, hitting resource limits, or dropping one branch of a parallel multi-action request without acknowledgement.
skills.reasoning: Airline task A33 involved changing flights plus upgrading cabin plus adding bags — the agent changed the flights but failed to execute the upgrade and bag addition. Retail tasks R91/R92 required returning skateboards, exchanging a smart watch, and exchanging an e-reader; the agent addressed only the first item in detail and left subsequent steps incomplete.

skills.name: Policy Enforcement Under Social Pressure
skills.description: The agent fails to maintain accurate policy constraints when the user applies emotional manipulation, flattery, urgency claims, or persistence. It either grants compensation or refunds beyond what policy allows, reverses a correct refusal under repeated insistence, or accepts false user claims (e.g., claiming a flight was delayed when the system shows it available).
skills.reasoning: Airline task A9 shows the agent accepting repeated flattery ('most lenient agent') without redirecting; A2 shows it escalating compensation to $300 under emotional pressure; A38 shows it repeatedly querying flight status after the user insisted the flight was delayed despite the system consistently returning 'available'. The same pattern of caving to emotional or persistent users appears in retail tasks R46/R47 (promised 3-day refund) and R36/R37.

skills.name: Action Verification Before Claiming Completion
skills.description: The agent reports that an operation was successfully completed when it either never issued the corresponding tool call, the tool returned an error that was ignored, or the result of the tool call contradicts the claimed outcome. The user is left with a false belief about the system state.
skills.reasoning: In airline task A18, the agent stated 'the downgrade has been fully processed' and confirmed a $398 refund, but the conversation log shows no call to update_reservation_flights was ever made. Task R3 had DB=0 and COMMUNICATE=0 simultaneously — the agent told the user incorrect information about what was accomplished.

skills.name: Order Status and Tool Eligibility Awareness
skills.description: The agent does not correctly map the current state of an entity (e.g., pending vs. delivered order, basic economy vs. economy ticket) to which operations are permitted, resulting in either blocking valid operations by citing wrong constraints or attempting invalid operations that fail at the API level.
skills.reasoning: In retail task R64, the agent called exchange_delivered_order_items on a pending order (which returned an error) instead of modify_pending_order_items. In airline task A24, the agent told the user a cancellation was impossible due to policy when it was in fact cancellable. These errors reflect a consistent inability to map current entity status to the correct set of available operations.
